content_of_post_to_comment: For generations, institutions helped decide who was credible before we ever encountered the person ourselves… They went to that university. Worked for that company. Were published by that publisher. Held that government position. Belonged to that political party. Practiced that religion. What will change as we no longer rely on those institutions to do so much of our evaluating for us?
comment: As institutions lose their role as credibility filters, we may gain access but also inherit the burden of judgment. The challenge shifts from trusting gatekeepers to developing better ways to evaluate people without defaulting to bias or popularity.
